correctness.rationale: Roots-of-unity orthogonality makes the normalized sampler an isometry. Erasing E subtracts the erased Gramian from I; dephasing each unnormalized erased row by ω^(−j) makes its row Gramian have diagonal 3 and kernel 1+2cos(2πs/N). For N≥8, |kernel|≤e at all circular distances ≥2. A nonconsecutive triple has at most one adjacent pair; after sorting that pair onto a d-edge, its absolute Gram matrix lies strictly below the consecutive matrix on at least one d-edge. The Rayleigh modulus inequality and irreducible nonnegative comparison give strict loss separation. For N=6,7 the nonadjacent absolute entries are at most 1, so the comparison matrix with edges (d,1,1) has top 3+(d+√(d²+8))/2, below 3+√2 d since d²≥4>2+√2. This is at most L_N. Reflection splits the consecutive block into the odd eigenvalue 3−e and two even roots, the upper of which is simple. Mapping (1,r,1) back by the dephased row adjoint yields precisely the stated centered coefficient vector; translation by t modulates coefficient k by exp(−2πitk/N). Full rank follows from a three-site retained Vandermonde minor, the endpoint follows from d=2,e=0, and expanding d=3−θ²+O(θ⁴), e=3−4θ²+O(θ⁴) yields L_N=9−4θ²+O(θ⁴). The inverse best conditioning factor is the stated reciprocal singular value.
residual_risks: Extremizers here mean nonzero signals in the residual-energy ratio. The zero vector gives vacuous equality in (1) for every mask; the proof sentence about only nonzero multiples should be read in the ratio sense. Finite floating-point checks do not prove the analytic result.
